---
title: "Eos"
subtitle: "Genesis Era (~12,630 SD)"
---


Prime body of a primary system, and a Tier 5 world where the dossier promised a
Tier 6. Settled by the Genesis ship whose Guide called itself Nova-136. Setting
of *My Children*.

## The star

Delta Pavonis: a G-type star 19.9 light-years from Sol, slightly older and
brighter than the Sun and beginning to leave the main sequence. One of the
`C-06` systems the Exodus thought worth three hulls.

## The world

- Gravity 1.16 standard. A heavier step, a shorter fall.
- Day of 26.7 standard hours; year of 478 local days.
- Free rotation, with seasons and a temperate band (`I-14`).
- About two thirds ocean.
- Breathable air, nitrogen and oxygen, with oxygen near 27 percent. That figure
  is what moves Eos from Tier 6 to Tier 5. It burns hotter, and over a lifetime
  it ages a human body faster than Earth air does.
- Abundant plant-like life, no animal-like life at landfall.

The dossier was assembled at Sol from thirty-light-year instruments and was
centuries stale on arrival (`C-16`). The oxygen figure was not in it.

## The native chemistry

Eos flora shares Earth's handedness and is digestible. Its dominant defensive
compound is an oxidant close in structure to the vicine of the fava bean, present
in most native plants and richest in the berries. Unmodified humans tolerate it.
Humans whose red-cell redox defences have been altered do not. See
[genesis-landfall](/encyclopedia/genesis-landfall.html) for why that mattered on Eos.

See also: [sagan-kim-scale](/encyclopedia/sagan-kim-scale.html), [cosmography](/encyclopedia/cosmography.html), [genesis-landfall](/encyclopedia/genesis-landfall.html).
